CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.

7498
SHANGHAI, 18th August 1936.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt
of your letter of 14th August 1936, No.D.7498,
concerning Amat bin Joeso, and thank you for
the information contained therein.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
〔签名〕
Chinese Secretary.

The Deputy Commissioner,
Crime & Special Branches,
SHANGHAI.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. D. 7498
Date 14 8 36

August 14 36.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of
your letter No. 2861 dated August 11, 1936, and in
reply to state that there is nothing in Police records
concerning Amat bin Joese. Enquiries show that Joese
is not living in the Municipal Work Shelter, but a few
days ago a man with a pock-marked face and having the
appearance of a Javanese called at the Work Shelter in
Amoy Road and requested assistance. None was given him
and he has not been back since.

I have the honour to be,

Sir,

Your obedient servant,

〔此处为手写签名〕

Deputy Commissioner
(Crime & Special Branches)

J. Van den Berg, Esq.,
Netherlands Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

Date August 13, 1936

Subject (in full) Enquiry from Netherlands Consulate General re Amat bin Joeso.

Made by D.S. Jones ........................................ Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I.

With reference to the letter dated August 11, 1936 from
the Netherlands Consulate General enquiring about a Javanese
named Amat bin Joeso, I have to state that there is nothing in
Police records regarding this individual.
Enquiries have been made at the Work Shelter now located
in the old Amoy Road gaol building, where Joeso is stated to
be living, but the principal of the Shelter declares that no
such person is staying on the premises. However, a few days
ago, a man short in stature described as having a pock-marked
face and who may have been a Javanese, called at the Work
Shelter in Amoy Road and requested assistance. None was given
him and he has not been back since.

D.S. Jones
D.S.

D.C. (Crime & Special Branches)

（左侧批注：O.R. / F.B.）

事由（全称） 荷兰总领事馆关于Amat bin Joeso之查询。

由 D.S. Jones 制作 ____ 由警司 J. Boyne 转呈

关于荷兰总领事馆19368月11日来函查询一名名为Amat bin Joeso的爪哇人一事，本人须声明，警方档案中并无关于此人之记录。
据称Joeso居住于现设于旧厦门路监狱大楼内的劳工收容所，已对该处进行查询，但收容所负责人宣称并无此人留宿。然而，数日前，一名身材矮小、被描述为面部有痘痕且可能为爪哇人的男子，曾前往厦门路劳工收容所请求援助。未予援助，此后该人未再返回。

D.S. Jones
侦探警佐

副巡官（犯罪股与特务股）

（左侧批注：O.R. / F.B.）

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 2861.

SHANGHAI, 11th August 1936.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2498
/3 8 36

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that a certain Amat bin
Joeso called at this Consulate General and applied for assistance.
He stated to have been born in Batavia, Tandjong Priok,
Java, in 1902, his parents being natives of Menado, who died a
long time ago.
About 1932 he stated to have left Java on one of the stea-
mers of the Java China Japan Line as a deckpassenger and went
to Shanghai to look for work, his profession being that of a
mechanic. According to his statement he stayed in Shanghai for
about 3½ years, during which time he did not succeed in finding
work.
He is supposed to have lived in lodging houses and accor-
ding to his statement he received occasionally money from
friends here.
At last he is said to have succeeded in leaving Shanghai
as a stowaway for Hongkong where, after a stay of a few months
he was arrested by the police as he was not in possession of a
passport.
He informed me that he visited the Netherlands Consulate
General in Hongkong and that the police, after having kept him
in custody for about 4 months, sent him back to Shanghai. He
is supposed to have stayed in Hongkong altogether for about
seven months and to have arrived in Shanghai about one month ago.
According to his statement he has been in possession of a
passport, issued at Batavia, which he lost a long time ago.
Pending inquiries in Hongkong and Batavia, Amat has been pro-
vided with a place in the Work Shelters of the Municipal Council.
I should feel greatly obliged to you if you would inform me
whether anything is known concerning this person, whose face

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / AUG. 1936 / (CRIME BRANCH)）
（批：S.2. / D.R. 12/8）

T. Robertson, Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

先生：

谨此通知阁下，某位Amat bin Joeso曾至本总领事馆请求援助。他声称于1902年出生在爪哇丹戎不碌（Tandjong Priok）的巴达维亚，其父母为万鸦老（Menado）土著，早已去世。
他声称约于1932年乘坐荷属东印度中国日本轮船公司（Java China Japan Line）的一艘轮船作为甲板乘客离开爪哇，前往上海寻找工作，其职业为机械师。据他陈述，他在上海停留了约三年半，在此期间未能找到工作。
据说他居住在客栈中，并据他陈述，偶尔从此地的朋友处获得金钱资助。
最后，据说他成功作为偷渡客离开上海前往香港，在那里停留数月后，因无护照被警方逮捕。
他告知我，他曾拜访荷兰驻香港总领事馆，警方在将其拘留约四个月后，将他遣返上海。据说他在香港总共停留了约七个月，并于约一个月前抵达上海。
据他陈述，他曾持有在巴达维亚签发的护照，但很久以前遗失。
在向香港和巴达维亚查询期间，已为Amat在市议会劳工收容所提供了一席之地。
如蒙告知是否知晓有关此人之任何情况，本人将不胜感激，其面容

（印：副巡官 / 1936年8月 / （犯罪股））
（批：S.2. / D.R. 12/8）

T. Robertson 先生，
主管特务股副巡官，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。
